172	
173	def _keys(
174	    value: dict, where: str, required: tuple[str, ...], optional: tuple[str, ...] = ()
175	) -> None:
176	    allowed = set(required) | set(optional)
177	    for key in value:
178	        if key not in allowed:
179	            raise ManifestError(f"{where}: unknown key {key!r}")
180	    for key in required:
181	        if key not in value:
182	            raise ManifestError(f"{where}.{key}: missing required key")
183	
184	
185	def _string(value: object, where: str) -> str:
186	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
187	        raise ManifestError(f"{where}: expected a non-empty string, found {value!r}")
188	    return value
189	
190	
191	def _number(value: object, where: str) -> float:
192	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
193	        raise ManifestError(f"{where}: expected a number, found {value!r}")
194	    return value

196	
197	def _list(value: object, where: str) -> list:
198	    if not isinstance(value, list):
199	        raise ManifestError(f"{where}: expected a list, found {type(value).__name__}")
200	    return value
201	
202	
203	def _unique(names: list[str], where: str, what: str) -> None:
204	    seen = set()
205	    for name in names:
206	        if name in seen:
207	            raise ManifestError(f"{where}: duplicate {what} {name!r}")
208	        seen.add(name)

211	def validate(data: object) -> dict:
212	    """Validate a study-package manifest. Raises :class:`ManifestError` on anything unexpected.
213	
214	    Every block is validated in full, including ``baseline`` and ``oracle``, which
215	    the indicator tool never reads — a malformed baseline is a failure at the first
216	    tool that opens the file, not a surprise for a later one.
217	    """
218	    root = _mapping(data, "manifest")
219	    _keys(
220	        root,
221	        "manifest",
222	        (
223	            "schema_version",
224	            "package",
225	            "fingerprints",
226	            "objective_catalog",
227	            "ties",
228	            "baseline",
229	            "oracle",
230	        ),
231	    )
232	    version = _string(root["schema_version"], "manifest.schema_version")
233	    if version != MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION:
234	        raise ManifestError(
235	            f"manifest.schema_version: expected {MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION!r}, found {version!r}"
236	        )
237	
238	    package = _mapping(root["package"], "manifest.package")
239	    _keys(package, "manifest.package", ("name", "path"))
240	    _string(package["name"], "manifest.package.name")
241	    _string(package["path"], "manifest.package.path")
242	
243	    _validate_fingerprints(root["fingerprints"])
244	    _validate_objective_catalog(root["objective_catalog"])
245	    _validate_ties(root["ties"])
246	    _validate_baseline(root["baseline"])
247	    _validate_oracle(root["oracle"])
248	    return root

250	
251	def _validate_fingerprints(value: object) -> None:
252	    block = _mapping(value, "manifest.fingerprints")
253	    _keys(block, "manifest.fingerprints", ("indicator_inputs", "recorded_provenance"))
254	
255	    pin = _mapping(block["indicator_inputs"], "manifest.fingerprints.indicator_inputs")
256	    where = "manifest.fingerprints.indicator_inputs"
257	    _keys(pin, where, ("recipe", "digest", "files"))
258	    recipe = _string(pin["recipe"], f"{where}.recipe")
259	    if recipe != INDICATOR_INPUT_RECIPE:
260	        raise ManifestError(
261	            f"{where}.recipe: expected {INDICATOR_INPUT_RECIPE!r}, found {recipe!r}"
262	        )
263	    _string(pin["digest"], f"{where}.digest")
264	    files = _list(pin["files"], f"{where}.files")
265	    if not files:
266	        raise ManifestError(f"{where}.files: must not be empty")
267	    for i, entry in enumerate(files):
268	        _string(entry, f"{where}.files[{i}]")
269	    _unique(files, f"{where}.files", "path")
270	    if list(files) != sorted(files):
271	        raise ManifestError(f"{where}.files: must be sorted by path")
272	
273	    prov = _mapping(block["recorded_provenance"], "manifest.fingerprints.recorded_provenance")
274	    where = "manifest.fingerprints.recorded_provenance"
275	    _keys(prov, where, ("executable_fingerprint", "semantic_fingerprint"))
276	    _string(prov["executable_fingerprint"], f"{where}.executable_fingerprint")
277	    _string(prov["semantic_fingerprint"], f"{where}.semantic_fingerprint")
278	
279	
280	def _validate_objective_catalog(value: object) -> None:
281	    entries = _list(value, "manifest.objective_catalog")
282	    if not entries:
283	        raise ManifestError("manifest.objective_catalog: must not be empty")
284	    for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
285	        where = f"manifest.objective_catalog[{i}]"
286	        obj = _mapping(entry, where)
287	        _keys(obj, where, ("name", "channel"), ("note",))
288	        _string(obj["name"], f"{where}.name")
289	        _string(obj["channel"], f"{where}.channel")
290	        if "note" in obj:
291	            _string(obj["note"], f"{where}.note")
292	    _unique([e["name"] for e in entries], "manifest.objective_catalog", "objective name")
293	    _unique([e["channel"] for e in entries], "manifest.objective_catalog", "objective channel")
294	
295	
296	def _validate_ties(value: object) -> None:
297	    entries = _list(value, "manifest.ties")
298	    for i, entry in enumerate(entries):
299	        where = f"manifest.ties[{i}]"
300	        tie = _mapping(entry, where)
301	        _keys(tie, where, ("key", "rides_with"), ("note",))
302	        _string(tie["key"], f"{where}.key")
303	        partners = _list(tie["rides_with"], f"{where}.rides_with")
304	        if not partners:
305	            raise ManifestError(f"{where}.rides_with: must not be empty")
306	        for j, partner in enumerate(partners):
307	            _string(partner, f"{where}.rides_with[{j}]")
308	        _unique(partners, f"{where}.rides_with", "key")
309	        if tie["key"] in partners:
310	            raise ManifestError(f"{where}: key {tie['key']!r} also appears in its own rides_with")
311	        if "note" in tie:
312	            _string(tie["note"], f"{where}.note")
313	    _unique([t["key"] for t in entries], "manifest.ties", "tie key")
314	
315	
316	def _validate_baseline(value: object) -> None:
317	    block = _mapping(value, "manifest.baseline")
318	    _keys(block, "manifest.baseline", ("point", "headline", "verdicts"))
319	
320	    point = _mapping(block["point"], "manifest.baseline.point")
321	    if not point:
322	        raise ManifestError("manifest.baseline.point: must not be empty")
323	    for key, val in point.items():
324	        _number(val, f"manifest.baseline.point[{key!r}]")
325	
326	    headline = _mapping(block["headline"], "manifest.baseline.headline")
327	    _keys(headline, "manifest.baseline.headline", ("channel", "value"))
328	    _string(headline["channel"], "manifest.baseline.headline.channel")
329	    _number(headline["value"], "manifest.baseline.headline.value")
330	
331	    verdicts = _list(block["verdicts"], "manifest.baseline.verdicts")
332	    if not verdicts:
333	        raise ManifestError("manifest.baseline.verdicts: must not be empty")
334	    for i, entry in enumerate(verdicts):
335	        where = f"manifest.baseline.verdicts[{i}]"
336	        verdict = _mapping(entry, where)
337	        _keys(verdict, where, ("source_local_identity", "expected"))
338	        _string(verdict["source_local_identity"], f"{where}.source_local_identity")
339	        expected = _string(verdict["expected"], f"{where}.expected")
340	        if expected not in ("satisfied", "violated"):
341	            raise ManifestError(
342	                f"{where}.expected: expected 'satisfied' or 'violated', found {expected!r}"
343	            )
344	    _unique(
345	        [v["source_local_identity"] for v in verdicts],
346	        "manifest.baseline.verdicts",
347	        "source_local_identity",
348	    )

351	def _validate_oracle(value: object) -> None:
352	    oracle = _mapping(value, "manifest.oracle")
353	    kind = _string(oracle.get("kind"), "manifest.oracle.kind")

356	    _keys(oracle, "manifest.oracle", ("kind", "module", "callable", "sys_path"), ("note",))

358	    _string(oracle["callable"], "manifest.oracle.callable")
359	    _string(oracle["sys_path"], "manifest.oracle.sys_path")
360	    if "note" in oracle:
361	        _string(oracle["note"], "manifest.oracle.note")

367	@dataclass(frozen=True)
368	class LoadedManifest:
369	    """A validated manifest plus the digest of the exact bytes it was read from."""
370	
371	    path: Path
372	    data: dict
373	    digest: str
374	
375	    @property
376	    def pinned_files(self) -> list[str]:
377	        return list(self.data["fingerprints"]["indicator_inputs"]["files"])
378	
379	    @property
380	    def pinned_digest(self) -> str:
381	        return self.data["fingerprints"]["indicator_inputs"]["digest"]
382	
383	
384	def load(path: Path | str) -> LoadedManifest:
385	    """Read, digest, parse, and validate a manifest file."""
386	    path = Path(path)
387	    try:
388	        raw = path.read_bytes()
389	    except OSError as exc:
390	        raise ManifestError(f"cannot read manifest {repo_relative_posix(path)}: {exc}") from exc
391	    try:
392	        data = json.loads(raw)
393	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
394	        raise ManifestError(
395	            f"manifest {repo_relative_posix(path)} is not valid JSON: {exc}"
396	        ) from exc
397	    validate(data)
398	    return LoadedManifest(path=path, data=data, digest=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest())

405	    """The live ``package_name`` from the package contract.
406	
407	    That contract file is deliberately outside the digested set — the trace never
408	    reads it — so the identity check can only refuse a run, never let one pass over
409	    unreviewed artifacts.
410	    """
411	    return _read_contract_field(
412	        Path(package_root) / "contracts" / "package_contract.json", "package_name"
413	    )

416	def read_executable_fingerprint(package_root: Path | str) -> str:

418	        Path(package_root) / "contracts" / "package_contract.json", "executable_fingerprint"
419	    )

422	def read_semantic_fingerprint(package_root: Path | str) -> str:

425	    )

428	def _read_contract_field(path: Path, field: str) -> str:
429	    try:
430	        raw = path.read_bytes()
431	    except OSError as exc:
432	        raise ManifestError(f"cannot read {repo_relative_posix(path)}: {exc}") from exc
433	    try:
434	        data = json.loads(raw)
435	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
436	        raise ManifestError(f"{repo_relative_posix(path)} is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
437	    if not isinstance(data, dict) or field not in data:
438	        raise ManifestError(f"{repo_relative_posix(path)}: missing {field!r}")
439	    return _string(data[field], f"{repo_relative_posix(path)}.{field}")

442	def assert_package_identity(manifest: LoadedManifest, package_root: Path | str) -> None:
443	    """The manifest must be the one authored for this package."""
444	    declared = manifest.data["package"]["name"]
445	    live = read_package_name(package_root)
446	    if declared != live:
447	        raise ManifestError(
448	            f"wrong manifest for this package: manifest package.name is {declared!r} but "
449	            f"contracts/package_contract.json package_name is {live!r}"
450	        )
451	
452	
453	def assert_pin_matches(manifest: LoadedManifest, computed: dict) -> None:
454	    """The pre-parse gate: the manifest's pin must equal the live indicator-input fingerprint."""
455	    if computed["digest"] == manifest.pinned_digest:
456	        return
457	    pinned_files = set(manifest.pinned_files)
458	    live_files = {f["path"] for f in computed["files"]}
459	    detail = [
460	        f"indicator-input fingerprint mismatch: manifest pins {manifest.pinned_digest} "
461	        f"but {INDICATOR_INPUT_RECIPE} over the live package is {computed['digest']}"
462	    ]
463	    added = sorted(live_files - pinned_files)
464	    removed = sorted(pinned_files - live_files)
465	    if added:
466	        detail.append(f"  files present but not pinned: {', '.join(added)}")
467	    if removed:
468	        detail.append(f"  files pinned but absent: {', '.join(removed)}")
469	    detail.append("  live per-file digests:")
470	    detail += [f"    {f['path']} {f['sha256']}" for f in computed["files"]]
471	    detail.append("  re-pin with --print-fingerprint after reviewing the change")
472	    raise ManifestError("\n".join(detail))
473	
474	
475	def assert_read_set_covered(
476	    resolved_paths: list[Path], package_root: Path | str, manifest: LoadedManifest
477	) -> None:
478	    """Every path the reader opened must sit inside the package and inside the pin (M3).
479	
480	    The reader resolves the inputs files from the pipeline's own EntryPoint refs, so a
481	    regenerated pipeline could point at a file the recipe never globbed — read by the
482	    trace, digested by nobody, pin still green. Both conditions fail closed.
483	    """
484	    root = Path(package_root).resolve()
485	    pinned = set(manifest.pinned_files)
486	    for path in resolved_paths:
487	        resolved = Path(path).resolve()
488	        if not resolved.is_relative_to(root):
489	            raise ManifestError(
490	                f"artifact resolves outside the package root: {resolved} "
491	                f"(package root {repo_relative_posix(root)})"
492	            )
493	        rel = package_relative_posix(resolved, root)
494	        if rel not in pinned:
495	            raise ManifestError(
496	                f"artifact read by the trace is not in the manifest's pinned file list: {rel}"
497	            )

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Conservative constraint/objective reachability for declared axis groups.
3	
4	Reads a generated teax package's own artifacts and reports, per author-declared
5	axis group, which constraints and objectives a conservative path can reach.
6	
7	Two layers, and the split is what makes the exit codes honest. The lower layer is
8	a pedantic reader: it loads the manifest, digests the artifacts it is about to read
9	and checks that digest against the manifest's pin, then parses the pipeline YAML
10	and the model contract in a mode where every unrecognized construct raises with a
11	location. Every failure there is mechanical, exits non-zero, and writes nothing.
12	The upper layer is the trace, and every outcome there is a fact that exits 0 —
13	including the empty one.
14	
15	The report is a document, not a stream: it is assembled in memory and written once,
16	after every gate has passed, so no code path can produce a partial report.
17	
18	The trace is deliberately over-approximate — every module output is taken to depend
19	on every module input. So a negative is sound (no finer analysis can find a path
20	this one missed) and a positive says only that the module graph admits a route.
21	
22	Usage:
23	    indicators.py --package DIR --manifest FILE --groups FILE [--group NAME]... [--out FILE]
24	    indicators.py --package DIR --print-fingerprint
25	
26	Generic by construction: this module names no package, no key prefix, and no
27	adapter (Invariant 6).
28	"""

105	
106	def _mapping_pairs(
107	    node: yaml.Node, path: Path, key_path: str, *, strict_tags: bool
108	) -> list[tuple[str, yaml.Node]]:
109	    """Ordered key/value pairs of a mapping node, with unique string keys.
110	
111	    ``strict_tags`` is on inside the ``modules`` subtree, where any node tag outside
112	    the standard str/map tags is a mechanical failure. An empty ``inputs:`` block
113	    composes to a null-tagged scalar rather than an empty mapping, so that is read
114	    as an empty map instead of raising.
115	    """
116	    if strict_tags and node.tag == _NULL_TAG:
117	        return []
118	    if not isinstance(node, yaml.MappingNode) or node.tag != _MAP_TAG:
119	        _fail(path, node, key_path, f"expected a mapping, found node tag {node.tag!r}")
120	    pairs: list[tuple[str, yaml.Node]] = []
121	    seen: set[str] = set()
122	    for key_node, value_node in node.value:
123	        if not isinstance(key_node, yaml.ScalarNode) or key_node.tag != _STR_TAG:
124	            _fail(path, key_node, key_path, f"expected a string key, found tag {key_node.tag!r}")
125	        key = key_node.value
126	        if key in seen:
127	            _fail(path, key_node, key_path, f"duplicate key {key!r}")
128	        seen.add(key)
129	        pairs.append((key, value_node))
130	    return pairs
131	
132	
133	def _scalar_string(node: yaml.Node, path: Path, key_path: str) -> str:
134	    if not isinstance(node, yaml.ScalarNode) or node.tag != _STR_TAG:
135	        _fail(path, node, key_path, f"expected a string scalar, found node tag {node.tag!r}")
136	    return node.value
137	
138	
139	def _read_ports(node: yaml.Node, path: Path, key_path: str) -> dict[str, Port]:
140	    ports: dict[str, Port] = {}
141	    for name, value_node in _mapping_pairs(node, path, key_path, strict_tags=True):
142	        where = f"{key_path}.{name}"
143	        value = _scalar_string(value_node, path, where)
144	        parts = value.split()
145	        if len(parts) != 2:
146	            _fail(path, value_node, where, f"cannot split type/ref in {value!r}")
147	        ports[name] = Port(type=parts[0], ref=parts[1], line=value_node.start_mark.line + 1)
148	    return ports

150	
151	def read_pipeline(path: Path) -> dict[str, Module]:
152	    """Parse one pipeline YAML with ``yaml.compose``, keeping line numbers.
153	
154	    Composing parses without constructing, so no tag can execute; but tags survive
155	    on nodes, so the walk asserts every tag inside the ``modules`` subtree. Every
156	    surprise raises with file, line, and key path.
157	    """
158	    try:
159	        root = yaml.compose(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
160	    except OSError as exc:
161	        rel = manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)
162	        raise IndicatorError(f"cannot read {rel}: {exc}") from exc
163	    except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
164	        raise IndicatorError(
165	            f"{manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)} is not valid YAML: {exc}"
166	        ) from exc
167	    if root is None:
168	        raise IndicatorError(f"{manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)} is empty")
169	
170	    top = dict(_mapping_pairs(root, path, "<root>", strict_tags=False))
171	    if set(top) != {"metadata", "modules"}:
172	        raise IndicatorError(
173	            f"{_where(path, root.start_mark.line + 1, '<root>')}: expected exactly the keys "
174	            f"'metadata' and 'modules', found {sorted(top)}"
175	        )
176	    # metadata gets a shape check only; nothing reads its contents.
177	    _mapping_pairs(top["metadata"], path, "metadata", strict_tags=False)
178	
179	    modules: dict[str, Module] = {}
180	    for name, body_node in _mapping_pairs(top["modules"], path, "modules", strict_tags=True):
181	        key_path = f"modules.{name}"
182	        body = dict(_mapping_pairs(body_node, path, key_path, strict_tags=True))
183	        unknown = sorted(set(body) - {"module_type", "inputs", "outputs"})
184	        if unknown:
185	            _fail(path, body_node, key_path, f"unknown key(s) {unknown}")
186	        if "module_type" not in body:
187	            _fail(path, body_node, key_path, "missing 'module_type'")
188	        modules[name] = Module(
189	            name=name,
190	            module_type=_scalar_string(body["module_type"], path, f"{key_path}.module_type"),
191	            inputs=(
192	                _read_ports(body["inputs"], path, f"{key_path}.inputs")
193	                if "inputs" in body
194	                else {}
195	            ),
196	            outputs=(
197	                _read_ports(body["outputs"], path, f"{key_path}.outputs")
198	                if "outputs" in body
199	                else {}
200	            ),
201	            line=body_node.start_mark.line + 1,
202	            file=path,
203	        )
204	    return modules
205

207	def _sole_module_of_type(
208	    modules: dict[str, Module], module_type: str, path: Path
209	) -> Module:
210	    found = sorted(m.name for m in modules.values() if m.module_type == module_type)
211	    if len(found) != 1:
212	        raise IndicatorError(
213	            f"{manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)}: expected exactly one {module_type} "
214	            f"module, found {len(found)}: {found}"
215	        )
216	    return modules[found[0]]

222	@dataclass
223	class PackageGraph:
224	    """The package-scoped channel graph, built across every pipeline file."""
225	
226	    modules: dict[str, Module] = field(default_factory=dict)
227	    entry_groups: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
228	    input_files: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
229	    producer: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
230	    deps: dict[str, dict[str, set[str]]] = field(default_factory=dict)
231	    input_keys: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
232	
233	
234	def classify_ref(raw: str, entry_groups: set[str], where: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
235	    """Normalize one input reference into ``('bound', key)`` or ``('channel', name)``.
236	
237	    R1 an entry-prefixed ``<group>.<key>`` is a bound input; R2 a bare ref is a
238	    produced channel; R3 a trailing ``.root`` is stripped (RootModel outputs declare a
239	    single field named ``root``, and 65 edges depend on the strip); R4 any other
240	    dotted ref is a hard failure, never guessed at and never silently dropped.
241	    """
242	    ref = raw.strip()
243	    head = ref.split(".", 1)[0]
244	    if head in entry_groups:
245	        rest = ref.split(".", 1)[1] if "." in ref else None
246	        if rest is None or "." in rest:
247	            raise IndicatorError(
248	                f"{where}: entry-prefixed reference is not '<group>.<key>': {raw!r}"
249	            )
250	        return "bound", rest
251	    if ref.endswith(".root"):
252	        ref = ref[: -len(".root")]  # R3: RootModel outputs declare a single field
253	    if "." in ref:
254	        raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: unparseable reference {raw!r}")
255	    return "channel", ref

258	@dataclass
259	class ParsedPipelines:
260	    """Every pipeline file, parsed, with the artifact paths the reader resolved.
261	
262	    Kept separate from the graph so the read-set coverage check (M3) runs between
263	    the two: the inputs files are named by the pipelines themselves, so they are
264	    checked against the manifest's pin before a single one of them is opened.
265	    """
266	
267	    modules: dict[str, Module] = field(default_factory=dict)
268	    entry_groups: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
269	    input_files: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
270	    pipeline_files: list[Path] = field(default_factory=list)
271	
272	    @property
273	    def artifact_paths(self) -> list[Path]:
274	        return [*self.pipeline_files, *self.input_files]
275	
276	
277	def read_pipelines(package_root: Path) -> ParsedPipelines:
278	    """Parse every ``pipelines/*.yaml`` and resolve the inputs files they declare.
279	
280	    Each file must carry exactly one EntryPoint and one ExitPoint (R11), and a module
281	    name may not appear in two files. Inputs paths come from the EntryPoint block's
282	    own refs, relative to the pipeline file's directory — never reconstructed.
283	    """
284	    parsed = ParsedPipelines()
285	    parsed.pipeline_files = sorted((package_root / "pipelines").glob("*.yaml"))
286	    if not parsed.pipeline_files:
287	        raise IndicatorError("no pipeline files at pipelines/*.yaml")
288	
289	    for path in parsed.pipeline_files:
290	        file_modules = read_pipeline(path)
291	        for name, module in file_modules.items():
292	            if name in parsed.modules:
293	                raise IndicatorError(
294	                    f"module {name!r} is declared in two pipeline files: "
295	                    f"{manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(parsed.modules[name].file)} and "
296	                    f"{manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)}"
297	                )
298	            parsed.modules[name] = module
299	        entry = _sole_module_of_type(file_modules, "EntryPoint", path)
300	        _sole_module_of_type(file_modules, "ExitPoint", path)
301	        for group, port in entry.inputs.items():
302	            parsed.entry_groups.add(group)
303	            resolved = (path.parent / port.ref).resolve()
304	            if resolved not in parsed.input_files:
305	                parsed.input_files.append(resolved)
306	    parsed.input_files.sort()
307	    return parsed
308	
309	
310	def build_graph(parsed: ParsedPipelines) -> PackageGraph:
311	    """Wire one package-scoped channel graph over every parsed module.
312	
313	    A channel produced by more than one module — same file or across files — is a
314	    mechanical failure.
315	    """
316	    graph = PackageGraph(
317	        modules=parsed.modules,
318	        entry_groups=parsed.entry_groups,
319	        input_files=parsed.input_files,
320	    )
321	    for module in graph.modules.values():
322	        if module.module_type in ("EntryPoint", "ExitPoint"):
323	            continue  # R11: neither participates in the closure
324	        bound: set[str] = set()
325	        channels: set[str] = set()
326	        for port_name, port in module.inputs.items():
327	            where = _where(module.file, port.line, f"modules.{module.name}.inputs.{port_name}")
328	            kind, value = classify_ref(port.ref, graph.entry_groups, where)
329	            (bound if kind == "bound" else channels).add(value)
330	        graph.deps[module.name] = {"bound": bound, "channels": channels}
331	        for port_name, port in module.outputs.items():
332	            where = _where(module.file, port.line, f"modules.{module.name}.outputs.{port_name}")
333	            if "." in port.ref:
334	                raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: output channel carries a field path: {port.ref!r}")
335	            if port.ref in graph.producer:
336	                raise IndicatorError(
337	                    f"{where}: channel {port.ref!r} is produced by more than one module: "
338	                    f"{graph.producer[port.ref]!r} and {module.name!r}"
339	                )
340	            graph.producer[port.ref] = module.name
341	
342	    for path in graph.input_files:
343	        for key in _read_input_keys(path):
344	            if key in graph.input_keys:
345	                raise IndicatorError(
346	                    f"input key {key!r} appears in two entry groups: "
347	                    f"{graph.input_keys[key]} and {manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)}"
348	                )
349	            graph.input_keys[key] = manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)
350	    return graph
351	
352	
353	def _read_input_keys(path: Path) -> list[str]:
354	    try:
355	        data = json.loads(path.read_bytes())
356	    except OSError as exc:
357	        raise IndicatorError(
358	            f"cannot read input file {manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)}: {exc}"
359	        ) from exc
360	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
361	        raise IndicatorError(
362	            f"input file {manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)} is not valid JSON: {exc}"
363	        ) from exc
364	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
365	        raise IndicatorError(
366	            f"input file {manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)}: expected an object of keys"
367	        )
368	    return list(data)

370	
371	def reachable_channels(
372	    declared: set[str], graph: PackageGraph
373	) -> tuple[set[str], set[str]]:
374	    """Conservative forward closure (R10).
375	
376	    A module fires if any declared key or any tainted channel is among its inputs,
377	    and firing taints all of its outputs. Iterated to fixpoint.
378	    """
379	    outputs_of: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
380	    for channel, module in graph.producer.items():
381	        outputs_of.setdefault(module, set()).add(channel)
382	
383	    tainted: set[str] = set()
384	    fired: set[str] = set()
385	    changed = True
386	    while changed:
387	        changed = False
388	        for module, dep in graph.deps.items():
389	            if module in fired:
390	                continue
391	            if (dep["bound"] & declared) or (dep["channels"] & tainted):
392	                fired.add(module)
393	                tainted |= outputs_of.get(module, set())
394	                changed = True
395	    return tainted, fired

450	def predicate_operands(entry: dict) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
451	    """The operator and ordered operand descriptors from ``predicate_ir`` (R7, R8).
452	
453	    Literal operands exist only here — they appear in no YAML and no input file.
454	    Any operand kind other than ``feature_ref`` or ``literal`` raises.
455	    """
456	    cid = entry["constraint_id"]
457	    try:
458	        ir = json.loads(entry["predicate_ir"])
459	    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
460	        raise IndicatorError(f"constraint {cid}: predicate_ir is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
461	    if ir.get("kind") != "operator":
462	        raise IndicatorError(f"constraint {cid}: predicate_ir root is not an operator")
463	    operands = []
464	    for operand in ir["operands"]:
465	        if operand["kind"] == "feature_ref":
466	            operands.append({"kind": "feature_ref", "name": operand["reference"]["source_name"]})
467	        elif operand["kind"] == "literal":
468	            operands.append({"kind": "literal", "value": operand["literal"]["value"]})
469	        else:
470	            raise IndicatorError(
471	                f"constraint {cid}: unknown predicate operand kind {operand['kind']!r}"
472	            )
473	    return ir["operator"], operands

493	def read_axis_declaration(path: Path) -> AxisDeclaration:
494	    """Read the per-study axis declaration. Every surprise is a mechanical failure."""
495	    rel = manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(path)
496	    try:
497	        raw = path.read_bytes()
498	    except OSError as exc:
499	        raise IndicatorError(f"cannot read axis declaration {rel}: {exc}") from exc
500	    try:
501	        data = json.loads(raw)
502	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
503	        raise IndicatorError(f"axis declaration {rel} is not valid JSON: {exc}") from exc
504	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
505	        raise IndicatorError(f"axis declaration {rel}: expected an object")
506	    unknown = sorted(set(data) - {"schema_version", "groups"})
507	    if unknown:
508	        raise IndicatorError(f"axis declaration {rel}: unknown key(s) {unknown}")
509	    version = data.get("schema_version")
510	    if version != AXIS_DECLARATION_SCHEMA_VERSION:
511	        raise IndicatorError(
512	            f"axis declaration {rel}: schema_version must be "
513	            f"{AXIS_DECLARATION_SCHEMA_VERSION!r}, found {version!r}"
514	        )
515	    raw_groups = data.get("groups")
516	    if not isinstance(raw_groups, list) or not raw_groups:
517	        raise IndicatorError(f"axis declaration {rel}: 'groups' must be a non-empty list")
518	
519	    groups: list[AxisGroup] = []
520	    seen_axes: set[str] = set()
521	    for i, raw_group in enumerate(raw_groups):
522	        where = f"axis declaration {rel}: groups[{i}]"
523	        if not isinstance(raw_group, dict):
524	            raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: expected an object")
525	        unknown = sorted(set(raw_group) - {"axis", "keys", "note"})
526	        if unknown:
527	            raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: unknown key(s) {unknown}")
528	        axis = raw_group.get("axis")
529	        if not isinstance(axis, str) or not axis:
530	            raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: 'axis' must be a non-empty string")
531	        if axis in seen_axes:
532	            raise IndicatorError(f"{where}: duplicate axis name {axis!r}")
533	        seen_axes.add(axis)
534	        raw_keys = raw_group.get("keys")
535	        if not isinstance(raw_keys, list) or not raw_keys:
536	            raise IndicatorError(f"{where} ({axis}): 'keys' must be a non-empty list")
537	        keys: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
538	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
539	        for j, raw_key in enumerate(raw_keys):
540	            key_where = f"{where} ({axis}): keys[{j}]"
541	            if not isinstance(raw_key, dict):
542	                raise IndicatorError(f"{key_where}: expected an object")
543	            unknown = sorted(set(raw_key) - {"key", "provenance"})
544	            if unknown:
545	                raise IndicatorError(f"{key_where}: unknown key(s) {unknown}")
546	            key = raw_key.get("key")
547	            provenance = raw_key.get("provenance")
548	            if not isinstance(key, str) or not key:
549	                raise IndicatorError(f"{key_where}: 'key' must be a non-empty string")
550	            if provenance not in ("fan_out", "tie"):
551	                raise IndicatorError(
552	                    f"{key_where}: 'provenance' must be 'fan_out' or 'tie', found {provenance!r}"
553	                )
554	            if key in seen_keys:
555	                raise IndicatorError(f"{key_where}: duplicate key {key!r} in group {axis!r}")
556	            seen_keys.add(key)
557	            keys.append((key, provenance))
558	        groups.append(AxisGroup(axis=axis, keys=keys))
559	
560	    return AxisDeclaration(
561	        path=path,
562	        digest=hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest(),
563	        schema_version=version,
564	        groups=groups,
565	    )

571	def resolve_declared_keys(
572	    group: AxisGroup, graph: PackageGraph, contract: ModelContract
573	) -> list[dict]:
574	    """Resolve each declared key to its entry type, in the order that makes each failure
575	    say the right thing: present in inputs, else a produced channel, else absent."""
576	    resolved = []
577	    for key, provenance in group.keys:
578	        if key in graph.input_keys:
579	            entry_type = contract.entry_types.get(key)
580	            if entry_type is None:
581	                raise IndicatorError(
582	                    f"axis {group.axis!r}: declared key {key!r} is present in inputs/ but is not "
583	                    f"in contract parameters, so its entry type cannot be classified"
584	                )
585	            resolved.append({"key": key, "provenance": provenance, "entry_type": entry_type})
586	        elif key in graph.producer:
587	            raise IndicatorError(
588	                f"axis {group.axis!r}: declared key {key!r} names a computed quantity — it is a "
589	                f"channel produced by module {graph.producer[key]!r}, not a bound input. A "
590	                f"computed quantity is a model output, not an axis."
591	            )
592	        else:
593	            raise IndicatorError(
594	                f"axis {group.axis!r}: declared key {key!r} is absent from the package inputs"
595	            )
596	    resolved.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["key"])
597	    return resolved

600	def _constraint_entry(
601	    entry: dict, graph: PackageGraph, contract: ModelContract, declared: set[str], tainted: set[str]
602	) -> dict:
603	    """One constraint under one axis. The same shape serves bounds and both partitions."""
604	    cid = entry["constraint_id"]
605	    module = graph.modules.get(cid)
606	    if module is None:
607	        raise IndicatorError(f"constraint {cid!r} has no matching module in the pipeline")
608	    operator, operands = predicate_operands(entry)
609	
610	    detail = []
611	    for operand in operands:
612	        if operand["kind"] == "literal":
613	            detail.append(
614	                {
615	                    "operand": "<literal>",
616	                    "class": "literal",
617	                    "reached": False,
618	                    "value": operand["value"],
619	                }
620	            )
621	            continue
622	        name = operand["name"]
623	        port = module.inputs.get(name)
624	        if port is None:
625	            raise IndicatorError(
626	                f"constraint {cid}: predicate operand {name!r} has no matching input port on "
627	                f"module {cid!r}"
628	            )
629	        where = _where(module.file, port.line, f"modules.{cid}.inputs.{name}")
630	        kind, value = classify_ref(port.ref, graph.entry_groups, where)
631	        operand_class = "bound" if kind == "bound" else "computed"
632	        reached = (value in declared) if kind == "bound" else (value in tainted)
633	        record = {"operand": name, "class": operand_class, "ref": value, "reached": reached}
634	        if kind == "bound":
635	            record["entry_type"] = contract.entry_types.get(value)
636	            if record["entry_type"] is None:
637	                raise IndicatorError(
638	                    f"constraint {cid}: bound operand {name!r} refers to {value!r}, which is not "
639	                    f"in contract parameters"
640	                )
641	        detail.append(record)
642	
643	    classes = sorted({d["class"] for d in detail if d["class"] != "literal"})
644	    return {
645	        "constraint_id": cid,
646	        "definition_qualified_name": entry["definition_qualified_name"],
647	        "source_local_identity": entry["source_local_identity"],
648	        "operator": operator,
649	        "operand_classes": classes,
650	        "bound_vs_bound": classes == ["bound"],
651	        "operands": detail,
652	    }
653	
654	
655	def suffix_siblings(declared_keys: list[str], graph: PackageGraph) -> list[str]:
656	    """Advisory only (R12): keys outside the group sharing a declared key's suffix.
657	
658	    Computed after the trace and never merged into the group. Suffixes are not
659	    identity — a tie whose suffix differs will never surface here, which is why
660	    membership is declared.
661	    """
662	    suffixes = {key.rsplit("__", 1)[-1] for key in declared_keys}
663	    declared = set(declared_keys)
664	    return sorted(
665	        key
666	        for key in graph.input_keys
667	        if key.rsplit("__", 1)[-1] in suffixes and key not in declared
668	    )
669	
670	
671	def tie_candidate_warnings(declared_keys: list[str], ties: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
672	    """Advisory only: a tie whose partners are all in the group while its key is not."""
673	    declared = set(declared_keys)
674	    warnings = []
675	    for tie in ties:
676	        if tie["key"] in declared:
677	            continue
678	        if set(tie["rides_with"]) <= declared:
679	            warnings.append(
680	                {
681	                    "kind": "tie_candidate",
682	                    "detail": (
683	                        f"the manifest declares {tie['key']!r} as riding with "
684	                        f"{', '.join(sorted(tie['rides_with']))}, all of which are in this group. "
685	                        f"Membership is declared-only, so the key was not added — declare it if "
686	                        f"it belongs."
687	                    ),
688	                }
689	            )
690	    return warnings
691	
692	
693	def trace_group(
694	    group: AxisGroup,
695	    graph: PackageGraph,
696	    contract: ModelContract,
697	    objective_catalog: list[dict],
698	    ties: list[dict],
699	) -> dict:
700	    """One group object: the resolved keys, the closure, and what it reached."""
701	    declared_keys = resolve_declared_keys(group, graph, contract)
702	    declared = {entry["key"] for entry in declared_keys}
703	    tainted, fired = reachable_channels(declared, graph)
704	
705	    bounds = sorted(
706	        (
707	            _constraint_entry(entry, graph, contract, declared, tainted)
708	            for entry in contract.concrete_entries
709	        ),
710	        key=lambda entry: entry["constraint_id"],
711	    )
712	    reachable = [c for c in bounds if any(o["reached"] for o in c["operands"])]
713	    unreachable = [c for c in bounds if not any(o["reached"] for o in c["operands"])]
714	
715	    objectives_reachable = sorted(
716	        obj["name"] for obj in objective_catalog if obj["channel"] in tainted
717	    )
718	    objectives_unreachable = sorted(
719	        obj["name"] for obj in objective_catalog if obj["channel"] not in tainted
720	    )
721	
722	    return {
723	        "axis": group.axis,
724	        "declared_keys": declared_keys,
725	        "group_valid": True,
726	        "no_constraint_response": not reachable,
727	        "constraints_reachable": reachable,
728	        "constraints_unreachable": unreachable,
729	        "bounds": bounds,
730	        "objectives_reachable": objectives_reachable,
731	        "objectives_unreachable": objectives_unreachable,
732	        "sibling_candidates": suffix_siblings(sorted(declared), graph),
733	        "trace_size": {"modules_fired": len(fired), "channels_tainted": len(tainted)},
734	        "warnings": tie_candidate_warnings(sorted(declared), ties),
735	        "not_derivable": NOT_DERIVABLE,
736	    }
737	
738	
739	# --------------------------------------------------------------- the document
740	
741	
742	def _document_warnings(
743	    loaded: manifest_mod.LoadedManifest, package_root: Path, groups: list[AxisGroup]
744	) -> list[dict]:
745	    """Cross-cutting facts that never gate: provenance drift and shared keys."""
746	    warnings = []
747	    recorded = loaded.data["fingerprints"]["recorded_provenance"]
748	    live = {
749	        "semantic_fingerprint": manifest_mod.read_semantic_fingerprint(package_root),
750	        "executable_fingerprint": manifest_mod.read_executable_fingerprint(package_root),
751	    }
752	    for name, live_value in sorted(live.items()):
753	        if recorded[name] != live_value:
754	            warnings.append(
755	                {
756	                    "kind": "provenance_drift",
757	                    "detail": (
758	                        f"manifest records {name} {recorded[name]} but the live package reports "
759	                        f"{live_value}. Provenance only — a record built from this run would "
760	                        f"state the wrong package revision."
761	                    ),
762	                }
763	            )
764	
765	    owners: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
766	    for group in groups:
767	        for key, _ in group.keys:
768	            owners.setdefault(key, []).append(group.axis)
769	    for key, axes in sorted(owners.items()):
770	        if len(axes) > 1:
771	            warnings.append(
772	                {
773	                    "kind": "duplicate_key_across_groups",
774	                    "detail": f"key {key!r} is declared in more than one group: {', '.join(axes)}",
775	                }
776	            )
777	    return warnings
778	
779	
780	def _assert_objective_channels_exist(objective_catalog: list[dict], graph: PackageGraph) -> None:
781	    for objective in objective_catalog:
782	        if objective["channel"] not in graph.producer:
783	            raise IndicatorError(
784	                f"objective {objective['name']!r}: channel {objective['channel']!r} is produced "
785	                f"by no module"
786	            )
787	
788	
789	def build_report(
790	    package_root: Path,
791	    loaded: manifest_mod.LoadedManifest,
792	    declaration: AxisDeclaration,
793	    selected: list[str],
794	) -> dict:
795	    """Run every gate, trace the selected groups, and assemble the whole document.
796	
797	    Gate order is fixed (D8): manifest schema (already done by the loader) →
798	    package identity → indicator-input fingerprint → pipeline parse → contract parse
799	    → declared-key resolution → trace. The read-set coverage check (M3) is one
800	    assertion after the parse; it does not disturb that order.
801	    """
802	    manifest_mod.assert_package_identity(loaded, package_root)
803	    fingerprint = manifest_mod.indicator_input_fingerprint(package_root)
804	    manifest_mod.assert_pin_matches(loaded, fingerprint)
805	
806	    parsed = read_pipelines(package_root)
807	    contract_path = package_root / "contracts" / "model_contract.json"
808	    manifest_mod.assert_read_set_covered(
809	        parsed.artifact_paths + [contract_path], package_root, loaded
810	    )
811	    graph = build_graph(parsed)
812	    contract = read_model_contract(package_root)
813	
814	    objective_catalog = [
815	        {"name": obj["name"], "channel": obj["channel"]}
816	        for obj in loaded.data["objective_catalog"]
817	    ]
818	    objective_catalog.sort(key=lambda obj: obj["name"])
819	    _assert_objective_channels_exist(objective_catalog, graph)
820	
821	    ties = loaded.data["ties"]
822	    declared_names = [group.axis for group in declaration.groups]
823	    if selected:
824	        unknown = sorted(set(selected) - set(declared_names))
825	        if unknown:
826	            raise IndicatorError(
827	                f"--group named axes that are not in the declaration: {', '.join(unknown)}"
828	            )
829	        traced = [g for g in declaration.groups if g.axis in set(selected)]
830	    else:
831	        traced = list(declaration.groups)
832	
833	    groups = sorted(
834	        (trace_group(g, graph, contract, objective_catalog, ties) for g in traced),
835	        key=lambda g: g["axis"],
836	    )
837	
838	    return {
839	        "schema_version": REPORT_SCHEMA_VERSION,
840	        "tool": {
841	            "path": manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(Path(__file__)),
842	            "source_digest": manifest_mod.tool_source_digest(),
843	        },
844	        "package": {
845	            "path": loaded.data["package"]["path"],
846	            "package_name": manifest_mod.read_package_name(package_root),
847	            "semantic_fingerprint": contract.semantic_fingerprint,
848	            "recorded_executable_fingerprint": manifest_mod.read_executable_fingerprint(
849	                package_root
850	            ),
851	            "indicator_input_fingerprint": fingerprint,
852	        },
853	        "manifest": {
854	            "path": manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(loaded.path),
855	            "schema_version": loaded.data["schema_version"],
856	            "digest": loaded.digest,
857	        },
858	        "axis_declaration": {
859	            "path": manifest_mod.repo_relative_posix(declaration.path),
860	            "schema_version": declaration.schema_version,
861	            "digest": declaration.digest,
862	            "groups_declared": sorted(declared_names),
863	            "subset": bool(selected),
864	        },
865	        "objective_catalog": objective_catalog,
866	        "not_derivable": NOT_DERIVABLE,
867	        "warnings": _document_warnings(loaded, package_root, declaration.groups),
868	        "groups": groups,
869	    }
870	
871	
872	def human_summary(report: dict) -> str:
873	    """The per-group summary that goes to stderr, so it can never contaminate stdout."""
874	    lines = []
875	    for group in report["groups"]:
876	        lines.append(
877	            f"{group['axis']}: "
878	            f"no_constraint_response={str(group['no_constraint_response']).lower()} "
879	            f"constraints {len(group['constraints_reachable'])}/{len(group['bounds'])} "
880	            f"objectives {len(group['objectives_reachable'])}/"
881	            f"{len(group['objectives_reachable']) + len(group['objectives_unreachable'])} "
882	            f"modules_fired={group['trace_size']['modules_fired']}"
883	        )
884	    lines.append(NOT_DERIVABLE["positive_reading"])
885	    return "\n".join(lines)
886	
887	
888	def write_atomically(text: str, out_path: Path) -> None:
889	    """Write via a temp file in the same directory, then rename."""
890	    temp = out_path.with_name(out_path.name + ".tmp")
891	    temp.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
892	    os.replace(temp, out_path)
893	
894	
895	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------- CLI
896	
897	
898	def print_fingerprint(package_root: Path) -> str:
899	    """The indicator-input fingerprint plus every per-file digest, as printable text."""
900	    computed = manifest_mod.indicator_input_fingerprint(package_root)
901	    lines = [f"recipe {computed['recipe']}", f"digest {computed['digest']}", "files"]
902	    lines += [f"  {f['path']} {f['sha256']}" for f in computed["files"]]
903	    return "\n".join(lines)
904	
905	
906	def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
907	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
908	        prog="indicators.py",
909	        description="Conservative constraint/objective reachability for declared axis groups.",
910	    )
911	    parser.add_argument("--package", required=True, metavar="DIR", help="package root directory")
912	    parser.add_argument("--manifest", metavar="FILE", help="study package manifest JSON")
913	    parser.add_argument("--groups", metavar="FILE", help="axis declaration JSON")
914	    parser.add_argument(
915	        "--group",
916	        action="append",
917	        default=[],
918	        metavar="NAME",
919	        help="trace only this axis (repeatable); a debugging aid — forces subset: true",
920	    )
921	    parser.add_argument("--out", metavar="FILE", help="write the report here instead of stdout")
922	    parser.add_argument(
923	        "--print-fingerprint",
924	        action="store_true",
925	        help="print the indicator-input fingerprint and per-file digests, then exit",
926	    )
927	    return parser
928	
929	
930	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
931	    parser = build_parser()
932	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
933	    package_root = Path(args.package)
934	
935	    if args.print_fingerprint:
936	        for unsupported in ("manifest", "groups", "out"):
937	            if getattr(args, unsupported):
938	                parser.error(f"--{unsupported} is not used with --print-fingerprint")
939	        if args.group:
940	            parser.error("--group is not used with --print-fingerprint")
941	    elif not args.manifest or not args.groups:
942	        parser.error("--manifest and --groups are required unless --print-fingerprint is given")
943	
944	    try:
945	        if args.print_fingerprint:
946	            print(print_fingerprint(package_root))
947	            return 0
948	        loaded = manifest_mod.load(Path(args.manifest))
949	        declaration = read_axis_declaration(Path(args.groups))
950	        report = build_report(package_root, loaded, declaration, args.group)
951	    except (IndicatorError, manifest_mod.ManifestError) as exc:
952	        print(str(exc), file=sys.stderr)
953	        return 1
954	
955	    text = json.dumps(report, indent=2) + "\n"
956	    print(human_summary(report), file=sys.stderr)
957	    if args.out:
958	        write_atomically(text, Path(args.out))
959	    else:
960	        sys.stdout.write(text)
961	    return 0
962	
963	
964	if __name__ == "__main__":
965	    sys.exit(main())

"""The exit-0 empty result: a fact, not a failure.

A broken analysis and an empty one must never share an exit code. This is the
empty one, and it exits 0 with a full report.
"""

import json

from tests.study.conftest import DATA_DIR, REAL_MANIFEST, REAL_PACKAGE, run_tool_raw

EXTRAS = DATA_DIR / "axes.extras.json"


def group_by_axis(doc, axis):
    return next(g for g in doc["groups"] if g["axis"] == axis)


def test_a_group_with_no_constraint_reach_exits_zero(tmp_path):
    out_path = tmp_path / "indicators.json"
    rc, out, err = run_tool_raw(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS, out=out_path)
    assert rc == 0, err
    assert out == ""  # --out was given, so the document went to the file
    doc = json.loads(out_path.read_text())

    group = group_by_axis(doc, "land_cost")
    assert group["group_valid"] is True
    assert group["no_constraint_response"] is True
    assert group["constraints_reachable"] == []
    assert group["objectives_reachable"] == ["lcoe", "lcoe_1cfe", "total_capital"]
    assert group["objectives_unreachable"] == ["cas72", "fuel"]


def test_the_empty_result_still_carries_the_whole_catalog(tmp_path):
    """Invariant 4 and 5: no_constraint_response is emitted with the full bounds
    list under this axis, so a reader sees what was checked, not just what was found."""
    rc, out, err = run_tool_raw(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    assert rc == 0, err
    group = group_by_axis(json.loads(out), "land_cost")
    assert len(group["bounds"]) == 5
    assert len(group["constraints_unreachable"]) == 5
    assert all(not any(o["reached"] for o in c["operands"]) for c in group["bounds"])


def test_no_constraint_response_is_emitted_even_when_false(tmp_path):
    rc, out, err = run_tool_raw(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    assert rc == 0, err
    doc = json.loads(out)
    for group in doc["groups"]:
        assert "no_constraint_response" in group
        assert group["no_constraint_response"] == (group["constraints_reachable"] == [])
    assert group_by_axis(doc, "R_partial")["no_constraint_response"] is False


def test_the_document_goes_to_stdout_and_the_summary_to_stderr():
    """The human summary can never contaminate the report."""
    rc, out, err = run_tool_raw(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    assert rc == 0
    json.loads(out)  # stdout is the document and nothing else
    assert "land_cost:" in err
    assert "possible path exists" in err

1	"""Invariant 6: generic and package-specific never share a file.
2	
3	The tool names no package, no key prefix, and no adapter. The manifest holds no
4	logic. This is the grep that keeps the two apart.
5	"""
6	
7	import pytest
8	
9	TOOL_MODULES = ["scripts/study/indicators.py", "scripts/study/manifest.py"]
10	PACKAGE_NAME = "stellarator_tea"
11	KEY_PREFIX = "stellarator_09__stellaris__"
12	
13	
14	@pytest.mark.parametrize("needle", [PACKAGE_NAME, KEY_PREFIX, "era_adapter"])
15	@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
16	def test_tool_modules_are_generic(needle, path, repo_root):
17	    assert needle not in (repo_root / path).read_text()
18	
19	
20	@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
21	def test_tool_modules_name_no_pipeline_or_objective_channel(path, repo_root):
22	    """The objective catalog is manifest-owned; no channel is hard-coded in the tool."""
23	    text = (repo_root / path).read_text()
24	    for needle in ("mfe_stellarator", "lcoe_calc", "verify_stellaris", "stellaris"):
25	        assert needle not in text
26	
27	
28	@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
29	def test_tool_modules_import_no_package_code(path, repo_root):
30	    text = (repo_root / path).read_text()
31	    assert "exploration" not in text
32	    assert "stellarator" not in text
33	
34	
35	@pytest.mark.parametrize("needle", ["import ", "lambda", "eval(", "exec(", "$ref", "!!"])
36	def test_the_manifest_holds_no_executable_content(needle, real_manifest_path):
37	    """The manifest is data only: no import hooks, no computed defaults."""
38	    assert real_manifest_path.suffix == ".json"
39	    assert needle not in real_manifest_path.read_text()
40	
41	
42	def test_the_tool_modules_exist_and_no_init(repo_root):
43	    """No __init__.py — implicit namespace packages plus pythonpath = ['.'] make the
44	    import work, and an empty module file would be a file nobody reads. Other epic

"""Invariant 6: generic and package-specific never share a file.

The tool names no package, no key prefix, and no adapter. The manifest holds no
logic. This is the grep that keeps the two apart.
"""

import pytest

TOOL_MODULES = ["scripts/study/indicators.py", "scripts/study/manifest.py"]
PACKAGE_NAME = "stellarator_tea"
KEY_PREFIX = "stellarator_09__stellaris__"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("needle", [PACKAGE_NAME, KEY_PREFIX, "era_adapter"])
@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
def test_tool_modules_are_generic(needle, path, repo_root):
    assert needle not in (repo_root / path).read_text()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
def test_tool_modules_name_no_pipeline_or_objective_channel(path, repo_root):
    """The objective catalog is manifest-owned; no channel is hard-coded in the tool."""
    text = (repo_root / path).read_text()
    for needle in ("mfe_stellarator", "lcoe_calc", "verify_stellaris", "stellaris"):
        assert needle not in text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", TOOL_MODULES)
def test_tool_modules_import_no_package_code(path, repo_root):
    text = (repo_root / path).read_text()
    assert "exploration" not in text
    assert "stellarator" not in text


@pytest.mark.parametrize("needle", ["import ", "lambda", "eval(", "exec(", "$ref", "!!"])
def test_the_manifest_holds_no_executable_content(needle, real_manifest_path):
    """The manifest is data only: no import hooks, no computed defaults."""
    assert real_manifest_path.suffix == ".json"
    assert needle not in real_manifest_path.read_text()


def test_the_tool_modules_exist_and_no_init(repo_root):
    """No __init__.py — implicit namespace packages plus pythonpath = ['.'] make the
    import work, and an empty module file would be a file nobody reads. Other epic
    items (preflight.py, verify.py, identity.py, common.py — Item 4) share this
    directory, so this test asserts presence, never an exact listing."""
    found = sorted(p.name for p in (repo_root / "scripts" / "study").glob("*.py"))
    assert {"indicators.py", "manifest.py"} <= set(found)
    assert not (repo_root / "scripts" / "study" / "__init__.py").exists()


def test_the_schema_files_are_the_committed_contract(repo_root):
    """Item 3's three schemas must exist; Item 4 adds its own to the same directory,
    so this is a subset assertion, not an exact listing."""
    found = sorted(p.name for p in (repo_root / "scripts" / "study" / "schemas").glob("*.json"))
    assert {
        "axis_declaration.v1.schema.json",
        "indicators.v1.schema.json",
        "study_package_manifest.v1.schema.json",
    } <= set(found)


def test_the_committed_package_is_untouched(repo_root):
    """The package under exploration/stellarator_e2e/pkg/ is read-only to this suite;
    every mutation test runs on a package_copy in tmp_path."""
    import subprocess

    done = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "status", "--porcelain", "exploration/stellarator_e2e/pkg"],
        cwd=str(repo_root), capture_output=True, text=True, check=True,
    )
    assert done.stdout == "", f"the committed package was modified:\n{done.stdout}"


def test_the_tool_resolves_its_own_repo_root():
    """Paths in the report come from __file__, never from the caller's working
    directory — that is what makes the document byte-identical across invocations."""
    from scripts.study import manifest

    root = manifest.repo_root()
    assert (root / "scripts" / "study" / "manifest.py").is_file()
    assert manifest.repo_relative_posix(root / "pyproject.toml") == "pyproject.toml"

    computed = manifest.indicator_input_fingerprint(real_package_path)

def test_tool_source_digest_recomputes(repo_root):

    computed = manifest.tool_source_digest()
    assert computed["recipe"] == "tool-source-digest/v1"
    lines = ["tool-source-digest/v1"] + [
        f"{rel} {hashlib.sha256((repo_root / rel).read_bytes()).hexdigest()}"
        for rel in sorted(manifest.TOOL_SOURCE_FILES)

@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "stem", ["indicators.v1", "study_package_manifest.v1", "axis_declaration.v1"]
)
def test_schemas_are_closed(stem, load_schema):
    """additionalProperties: false throughout — the citable contract is exact."""
    schema = load_schema(stem)

    def walk(node):
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            if node.get("type") == "object" and "additionalProperties" not in node:
                raise AssertionError(f"{stem}: open object at {node.get('title', node)}")
            for value in node.values():
                walk(value)
        elif isinstance(node, list):
            for value in node:
                walk(value)

    walk(schema)

def test_constraint_completeness(real_package_path):
    """Invariant 5 / S4: both halves. Every catalog constraint appears exactly once
    in bounds and exactly once across reachable + unreachable."""
    contract = json.loads(
        (real_package_path / "contracts" / "model_contract.json").read_text()
    )
    catalog_ids = sorted(
        e["constraint_id"] for e in contract["constraint_catalog"]["concrete_entries"]
    )
    for group in _report()["groups"]:
        assert sorted(c["constraint_id"] for c in group["bounds"]) == catalog_ids
        partition = group["constraints_reachable"] + group["constraints_unreachable"]
        assert sorted(c["constraint_id"] for c in partition) == catalog_ids


def test_bounds_is_authoritative_and_axis_varying():
    """S2: the two partition lists are bounds filtered on 'any operand reached'."""
    doc = _report()
    for group in doc["groups"]:
        reachable = [c for c in group["bounds"] if any(o["reached"] for o in c["operands"])]
        assert reachable == group["constraints_reachable"]
        unreachable = [
            c for c in group["bounds"] if not any(o["reached"] for o in c["operands"])
        ]
        assert unreachable == group["constraints_unreachable"]
    by_axis = {g["axis"]: g["bounds"] for g in doc["groups"]}
    assert by_axis["R"] != by_axis["beta"]  # bounds vary per axis, not a constant block


def test_lists_are_sorted_by_a_stated_key():
    """D4: deterministic order, no set-iteration leaking through."""
    doc = _report()
    assert [g["axis"] for g in doc["groups"]] == sorted(g["axis"] for g in doc["groups"])
    assert [o["name"] for o in doc["objective_catalog"]] == sorted(

    assert "generated_at" not in text

"""Advisory is advisory: warnings never change which keys are traced.

Invariant 3. A group with warnings and the same group with the manifest tie
removed produce identical trace fields.
"""

import json

from tests.study.conftest import DATA_DIR, REAL_MANIFEST, REAL_PACKAGE, run_tool

EXTRAS = DATA_DIR / "axes.extras.json"

TRACE_FIELDS = (
    "declared_keys",
    "constraints_reachable",
    "constraints_unreachable",
    "bounds",
    "objectives_reachable",
    "objectives_unreachable",
    "trace_size",
    "no_constraint_response",
    "sibling_candidates",
)


def group_by_axis(doc, axis):
    return next(g for g in doc["groups"] if g["axis"] == axis)


def trace_fields(doc, axis):
    group = group_by_axis(doc, axis)
    return {field: group[field] for field in TRACE_FIELDS}


def warning_kinds(doc, axis):
    return sorted(w["kind"] for w in group_by_axis(doc, axis)["warnings"])


def test_advisory_never_changes_the_trace(package_copy):
    """Remove the manifest's tie catalog entry: the warning goes, the trace does not
    move a single field."""
    with_tie = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    copy = package_copy(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    copy.edit_manifest(lambda data: data.update(ties=[]))
    rc, out, err = copy.run()
    assert rc == 0, err
    without_tie = json.loads(out)

    assert trace_fields(with_tie, "R_partial") == trace_fields(without_tie, "R_partial")
    assert warning_kinds(with_tie, "R_partial") == ["tie_candidate"]
    assert warning_kinds(without_tie, "R_partial") == []


def test_the_tie_candidate_names_the_key_and_says_it_was_not_added():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    (warning,) = group_by_axis(doc, "R_partial")["warnings"]
    assert warning["kind"] == "tie_candidate"
    assert "magnet__R0" in warning["detail"]
    assert "not added" in warning["detail"]


def test_a_declared_tie_earns_no_candidate_warning():
    """The tie is already in the group, so there is nothing to suggest."""
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, DATA_DIR / "axes.known_answers.json")
    assert warning_kinds(doc, "R+tie") == []
    assert warning_kinds(doc, "R") == ["tie_candidate"]


def test_suffix_siblings_land_in_their_own_named_field():
    """M2: sibling_candidates is an Appendix A name and is never folded into
    warnings — there is exactly one place to read them."""
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    group = group_by_axis(doc, "n_mod")
    assert len(group["sibling_candidates"]) == 17  # 18 keys share the suffix, 1 declared
    assert all(key.endswith("__n_mod") for key in group["sibling_candidates"])
    assert group["sibling_candidates"] == sorted(group["sibling_candidates"])
    assert warning_kinds(doc, "n_mod") == []
    assert "sibling" not in json.dumps(group["warnings"])


def test_suffix_siblings_never_join_the_traced_set():
    """Invariant 3: 17 candidates, 1 traced key."""
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    group = group_by_axis(doc, "n_mod")
    assert len(group["declared_keys"]) == 1
    assert group["sibling_candidates"]


def test_the_declared_tie_is_not_a_suffix_sibling():
    """The concrete demonstration that suffixes are not identity: magnet__R0 has
    suffix R0, so no suffix scan will ever surface it — the tie must be declared."""
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    siblings = group_by_axis(doc, "R_partial")["sibling_candidates"]
    assert not any(key.endswith("magnet__R0") for key in siblings)


def test_a_key_in_two_groups_earns_a_document_warning():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    duplicates = [w for w in doc["warnings"] if w["kind"] == "duplicate_key_across_groups"]
    assert len(duplicates) == 1
    assert "geom__R" in duplicates[0]["detail"]
    assert "R_partial" in duplicates[0]["detail"] and "R_shared" in duplicates[0]["detail"]


def test_provenance_drift_warns_on_both_recorded_fingerprints(package_copy):
    """S5: the drift case is a re-pin that left recorded_provenance stale. Neither
    fingerprint gates — gating on either is the false gate the spec ruled out."""
    copy = package_copy(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, EXTRAS)
    copy.edit_manifest(
        lambda data: data["fingerprints"]["recorded_provenance"].update(
            semantic_fingerprint="stale" * 12, executable_fingerprint="alsostale" * 7
        )
    )
    rc, out, err = copy.run()
    assert rc == 0, err  # provenance never gates
    drift = [w for w in json.loads(out)["warnings"] if w["kind"] == "provenance_drift"]
    assert len(drift) == 2
    assert any("executable_fingerprint" in w["detail"] for w in drift)
    assert any("semantic_fingerprint" in w["detail"] for w in drift)

the trace, digested by nobody, pin still green. Two conditions, both fail-closed.

Each copy is re-pinned before the run, so these tests reach the coverage check
rather than stopping at the pre-parse fingerprint gate.
"""

import json

from scripts.study import manifest

PIPELINE = "pipelines/mfe_stellarator.yaml"
ENTRY_REF = "system_design: SystemDesign ../inputs/system_design.json"


def test_a_ref_outside_the_pinned_file_list_fails(real_copy, tmp_path):
    """The file is inside the package and readable, but no digest covers it."""
    (real_copy.path / "handwritten" / "params.json").write_text(
        (real_copy.path / "inputs" / "system_design.json").read_text()
    )
    real_copy.edit(
        PIPELINE, ENTRY_REF, "system_design: SystemDesign ../handwritten/params.json"
    )
    out_path = tmp_path / "indicators.json"
    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(out=out_path)
    assert rc != 0
    assert "not in the manifest's pinned file list" in err
    assert "handwritten/params.json" in err
    assert out == ""
    assert not out_path.exists()


def test_a_ref_outside_the_package_root_fails(real_copy, tmp_path):
    outside = real_copy.path.parent / "outside.json"
    outside.write_text((real_copy.path / "inputs" / "system_design.json").read_text())
    real_copy.edit(PIPELINE, ENTRY_REF, "system_design: SystemDesign ../../outside.json")
    out_path = tmp_path / "indicators.json"
    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(out=out_path)
    assert rc != 0
    assert "resolves outside the package root" in err
    assert out == ""
    assert not out_path.exists()


def test_the_coverage_check_runs_before_the_inputs_are_opened(real_copy, tmp_path):
    """A file outside the package root is refused by path, not after being read."""
    outside = real_copy.path.parent / "not_even_json.txt"
    outside.write_text("this is not JSON at all")
    real_copy.edit(PIPELINE, ENTRY_REF, "system_design: SystemDesign ../../not_even_json.txt")
    _, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "x.json")
    assert "resolves outside the package root" in err
    assert "not valid JSON" not in err


def test_the_pinned_file_list_covers_exactly_what_the_reader_opens(real_package_path):
    """The invariant stated positively on the committed package."""
    from scripts.study import indicators

    parsed = indicators.read_pipelines(real_package_path)
    opened = {
        manifest.package_relative_posix(p, real_package_path)
        for p in parsed.artifact_paths
    } | {"contracts/model_contract.json"}
    pinned = {
        f["path"] for f in manifest.indicator_input_fingerprint(real_package_path)["files"]
    }
    assert opened == pinned


def test_pipelines_init_py_does_not_fail_the_glob_gate(real_package_path):
    """M1: __init__.py is a sealed artifact of every generated package. A rule that
    refused it would refuse the only package that exists."""
    assert (real_package_path / "pipelines" / "__init__.py").is_file()
    files = [f["path"] for f in manifest.indicator_input_fingerprint(real_package_path)["files"]]
    assert "pipelines/__init__.py" not in files


def test_a_renamed_inputs_file_is_followed_not_guessed(real_copy, tmp_path):
    """The reader resolves the EntryPoint's declared path rather than reconstructing
    inputs/<group>.json, so a rename is followed — and then caught by the pin."""
    (real_copy.path / "inputs" / "renamed.json").write_text(
        (real_copy.path / "inputs" / "system_design.json").read_text()
    )
    (real_copy.path / "inputs" / "system_design.json").unlink()
    real_copy.edit(PIPELINE, ENTRY_REF, "system_design: SystemDesign ../inputs/renamed.json")
    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "y.json")
    assert rc == 0, err
    report = json.loads((tmp_path / "y.json").read_text())
    files = [f["path"] for f in report["package"]["indicator_input_fingerprint"]["files"]]
    assert "inputs/renamed.json" in files
    assert "inputs/system_design.json" not in files

    path = copy.path / "inputs" / "system_design.json"
    data = json.loads(path.read_text())
    assert UNCLASSIFIED_KEY not in data, "fixture key already exists in the package"
    data[UNCLASSIFIED_KEY] = 1.0
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n")
    _declare(copy, UNCLASSIFIED_KEY)


def fingerprint_mismatch(copy):
    copy.edit(PIPELINE, "run_description:", "run_description:  ")


def unparseable_reference(copy):
    copy.edit(
        PIPELINE,
        "wall_load: float stellarator_09__stellaris__wall_load_calc__wall_load.root",
        "wall_load: float stellarator_09__stellaris__wall_load_calc__wall_load.value.deep",
    )


def corrupt_pipeline_line(copy):
    copy.edit(
        PIPELINE,
        "R: float system_design.stellarator_09__stellaris__geom__R",
        "R: floatonly_one_token",
    )


def ghost_objective_channel(copy):
    copy.edit_manifest(
        lambda data: data["objective_catalog"][0].update(channel="stellarator_09__no_such_channel")
    )


def wrong_manifest_for_package(copy):
    copy.edit_manifest(lambda data: data["package"].update(name="some_other_package"))


def malformed_manifest_baseline(copy):
    copy.edit_manifest(lambda data: data["baseline"]["headline"].update(value="two dollars"))


CASES = [
    ("missing_declared_key", missing_declared_key, ABSENT_KEY, True),
    ("key_names_produced_channel", key_names_produced_channel, "computed quantity", True),
    ("unclassifiable_key", unclassifiable_key, "not in contract parameters", True),
    ("fingerprint_mismatch", fingerprint_mismatch, "indicator-input fingerprint", False),
    ("unparseable_reference", unparseable_reference, "wall_load.value.deep", True),
    ("corrupt_pipeline_line", corrupt_pipeline_line, "mfe_stellarator.yaml:", True),
    ("ghost_objective_channel", ghost_objective_channel, "produced by no module", True),
    ("wrong_manifest_for_package", wrong_manifest_for_package, "package_name", True),
    ("malformed_manifest_baseline", malformed_manifest_baseline, "baseline", True),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "name,mutate,expect,repin", CASES, ids=[case[0] for case in CASES]
)
def test_fails_closed(real_copy, name, mutate, expect, repin, tmp_path):
    mutate(real_copy)
    out_path = tmp_path / "indicators.json"
    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(repin=repin, out=out_path)
    assert rc != 0, f"{name} exited 0"
    assert expect in err, f"{name}: message does not locate the fault:\n{err}"
    assert out == ""
    assert not out_path.exists()  # Invariant 1


def test_the_absent_key_and_the_computed_quantity_say_different_things(real_copy, tmp_path):
    """An author told 'your key is missing' when they picked a model output goes
    looking in the wrong place."""
    missing_declared_key(real_copy)
    _, _, absent = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "a.json")
    assert "absent from the package inputs" in absent
    assert "computed quantity" not in absent


def test_the_computed_quantity_message_names_the_producing_module(real_copy, tmp_path):
    key_names_produced_channel(real_copy)
    _, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "b.json")
    assert COMPUTED_QUANTITY in err
    assert "computed quantity" in err
    assert "channel produced by module" in err


def test_the_corrupt_line_carries_file_line_and_key_path(real_copy, tmp_path):
    corrupt_pipeline_line(real_copy)
    _, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "c.json")
    assert "mfe_stellarator.yaml:24" in err
    assert "key path modules.stellarator_09__stellaris__geom.inputs.R" in err
    assert "floatonly_one_token" in err


def test_the_fingerprint_mismatch_names_the_live_digests(real_copy, tmp_path):
    fingerprint_mismatch(real_copy)
    _, _, err = real_copy.run(repin=False, out=tmp_path / "d.json")
    assert "manifest pins" in err
    assert "live per-file digests" in err
    assert "pipelines/mfe_stellarator.yaml" in err
    assert "--print-fingerprint" in err


def test_the_ghost_objective_names_the_channel(real_copy, tmp_path):
    ghost_objective_channel(real_copy)
    _, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "e.json")
    assert "stellarator_09__no_such_channel" in err


def test_a_nonstandard_node_tag_inside_modules_is_a_failure(real_copy, tmp_path):
    """S6: compose preserves node tags, so a tagged value must be refused rather
    than read. Nothing executes either way — compose does not construct."""
    real_copy.edit(
        PIPELINE,
        "R: float system_design.stellarator_09__stellaris__geom__R",
        "R: !!python/object/apply:os.system ['echo pwned']",
    )
    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "f.json")
    assert rc != 0
    assert "node tag" in err
    assert out == ""


def test_an_unknown_key_inside_a_module_is_a_failure(real_copy, tmp_path):
    real_copy.edit(
        PIPELINE,
        "  stellarator_09__stellaris__geom:\n    module_type:",
        "  stellarator_09__stellaris__geom:\n    surprise: true\n    module_type:",
    )
    rc, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "g.json")

    assert "unknown key(s)" in err and "surprise" in err

    real_copy.edit_axes(lambda data: data["groups"].append(dict(data["groups"][0])))
    rc, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "h.json")
    assert rc != 0
    assert "duplicate axis name" in err


def test_an_unknown_provenance_is_a_failure(real_copy, tmp_path):
    real_copy.edit_axes(
        lambda data: data["groups"][0]["keys"][0].update(provenance="because_i_said_so")
    )
    rc, _, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "i.json")
    assert rc != 0
    assert "'fan_out' or 'tie'" in err

    rc, out, err = real_copy.run(out=tmp_path / "j.json", group=("no_such_axis",))
    assert rc != 0
    assert "no_such_axis" in err
    assert out == ""
    assert not (tmp_path / "j.json").exists()

"""S1 / Invariant 11: a subset run cannot pass for a complete one.

The record-feeding invocation traces every group in the declaration and emits
`subset: false`. `--group` is a debugging aid and always emits `subset: true`, so
a record reader can see the difference mechanically instead of trusting a runbook.
"""

import hashlib

from tests.study.conftest import DATA_DIR, REAL_MANIFEST, REAL_PACKAGE, run_tool

KNOWN_ANSWERS = DATA_DIR / "axes.known_answers.json"
ALL_AXES = ["R", "R+tie", "a", "availability", "beta", "interest_rate"]


def test_a_full_run_covers_the_whole_declaration():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS)
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["subset"] is False
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["groups_declared"] == ALL_AXES
    assert [g["axis"] for g in doc["groups"]] == ALL_AXES


def test_a_group_run_is_visibly_narrower():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS, group=("R",))
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["subset"] is True
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["groups_declared"] == ALL_AXES  # still the whole file
    assert [g["axis"] for g in doc["groups"]] == ["R"]


def test_several_groups_can_be_selected():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS, group=("beta", "R"))
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["subset"] is True
    assert [g["axis"] for g in doc["groups"]] == ["R", "beta"]


def test_a_subset_group_is_byte_identical_to_its_full_run_counterpart():
    """The debugging aid answers the same question, just about fewer axes."""
    full = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS)
    subset = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS, group=("beta",))
    assert next(g for g in full["groups"] if g["axis"] == "beta") == subset["groups"][0]


def test_the_axis_declaration_digest_matches_the_file_bytes():
    doc = run_tool(REAL_PACKAGE, REAL_MANIFEST, KNOWN_ANSWERS)
    expected = hashlib.sha256(KNOWN_ANSWERS.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["digest"] == expected
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["schema_version"] == "study-axis-declaration/v1"
    assert doc["axis_declaration"]["path"] == "tests/study/data/axes.known_answers.json"

2	
3	Invariant 8. A tie key and a fan-out key are traced identically; what provenance
4	changes is what a cold reader can tell about why the key is in the group.
5	"""
6	
7	from tests.study.conftest import DATA_DIR, REAL_MANIFEST, REAL_PACKAGE, run_tool
8

10	
11

13	    return next(g for g in doc["groups"] if g["axis"] == axis)
14	
15
